questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:

questions.answer: It was alright to find the information needed, but NTNU is not very good at helping international students. I had a lot of trouble finding available courses, because it was not obvious which courses where available for international students. But NTNU is very informative besides this.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
When you are from scandinavia, it was pretty easy. I think because of the language.
Hybel.no
and
finn.no
is very good to find accomondation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
When you are from scandinavia, you have huge advantage. 
Many private housings have a rental period for 1 whole year, and this contract can usually not be shorter (like 4 months). This can be a problem, when you are only there for a semester. I rented a room for a whole year, and then subletted the room to another student, the rest of the year. You can find subletted rooms, but it is a lot harder. This is a huge disadvantage of private housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You dont have to do anything, when you are from scandinavia and only staying for 1 semester.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All I had to do, was change my post adress.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
There was a lot of trouble, and I they kept sending me to other people, who couldn't help me either. I was told that I personally had to ask the professor, if I could join the course, but the professors where not aware of this. 
There was a lot of mis-communication. 
There is nowhere where you can see which courses are available to exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about having it figured out before you arrive, because you can register and unregister as you want for the first 3 weeks or so. So you can try the courses before deciding.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course level is similar to the ones at my host university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it was a lot similar. the only difference was, that you often had to hand in a paper or do a presentation, before being able to take the exam. I am not used to this from UCPH, but it was not hard to pass this test/paper/presentation. There was more mandatory classes than I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Molecular biology, Immunology, Molecular cell biology and genetics and Evolution I.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Immunology, Molecular cell biology

questions.answer: There are many trips and NTNUi cabins nearby, which is nice to visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, you just had to get use to the restrictions and that everything was closed on sundays. Also, tha alcohol culture is very different. You cannot buy alcohol at any time, and you always have to show ID. But otherwise, it is not that much of af difference.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you want to socialize with other internationals, it is a good ide to join "samfundet" or become a worker/ volunteer at "uka". Also NTNUi teams is a good way to do this.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the party culture and the food culture is veri different. Many Norwegian students do not cook much themselves, and are not used to this.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The bouldering community.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is more expensive that you expect. 
It is normal to have bad days.
Dont be scared to do something you usually wouldn't do. You fill find yourself in weird situations, but try to enjoy and see the fun in it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to take initiative.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Getting to know nice people, and learning to just accept the weird situations you'll be in. 
To find out, that you can actually do it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To establish an everyday-life and get a proper routine, and then, after a couple of moths, having to stop it all again.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
